newsitem.title: GREECE: FX swap rates rise prompt Bank of Greece dlr sales.
newsitem.headline: FX swap rates rise prompt Bank of Greece dlr sales.

text.p: Greek depos held Thursday's levels, but forex swaps traded 30 forward points higher as foreign traders actively took profits and closed positions and the central bank sold dollars for drachmas, dealers said.

"Forex swaps trade higher 30 pips with six-month swaps up 40 pips as some foreign players seek to close out positions and take profit, which prompted the Bank of Greece to sell dollars for drachmas," said a dealer at a state bank. "Depos started steady and are holding."
Traders estimated the amount of swaps turnover was more than 150 million dollars.
They also noted spot purchases of dollars for drachmas by overseas investors.
Bank of Greece cut its intervention bid in overnight funds by 20 basis points to 12.40 percent as July M3 and credit growth showed slowdowns on Thursday.
July M3 growth fell to 8.3 year-on-year from June's 9.0 percent to stay in the central bank's 6.0-9.0 percent target.
Dealers said the rate cut was aimed to discourage inflows through forex swaps, which have augmented interbank liquidity, and help the finance minsitry's T-bill issue on Monday.
Monday's T-bill issue will feature a 10 basis point cut in rates. The 12-month, six-month and three-month T-bills will fall to 12.70 percent, 12.10 percent and 11.90 percent, respectively.
Early elections will be on September 22, but the market was complacent, believing the winner will continue with Greece's EU convergence plan.
The mark was quoted at 160.08/13 drachmas from Thursday's 160.140 fix, the dollar at 236.55/65 drachmas from 236.460 and the Ecu at 301.07/17 from 301.130 drachmas.
